full_text_en:
Alimuradov Shamil Haji-ogly — Aircraft Hijacking Case

**Defendant:** Alimuradov Shamil Haji-ogly (Алимурадов Шамиль Гаджи-оглы), male, 33 years old, nationality of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, formerly residing at 19-2 Mazhesky Street, Yakutsk, Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, formerly deputy pilot of the United Flight Team of the Yakutsk Civil Aviation Administration of the Yakut Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic.

**Defense Counsel:** Wu Lianfen, lawyer from the First Legal Advisory Office of Harbin, Heilongjiang Province.

**Interpreters:** Yuan Changzai, Jin Guangyu, Guo Chenguang, Zhang Youzheng.

The defendant Alimuradov Shamil Haji-ogly was indicted for aircraft hijacking by the Harbin People's Procuratorate of Heilongjiang Province before the Harbin Intermediate People's Court. The Harbin Intermediate People's Court examined the case in accordance with Article 108 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Upon examination, it was determined that the People's Republic of China has jurisdiction over the case of the defendant Alimuradov Shamil Haji-ogly hijacking an aircraft. The basis is: In January 1978 and October 1980, the Chinese government respectively acceded to the Tokyo Convention, the Hague Convention, and the Montreal Convention, international conventions against the terrorist act of hijacking civil aircraft. The Circular of the General Office of the State Council concerning China's accession to these "Conventions" states: "If foreign aircraft are hijacked and land in China or other related foreign affairs incidents occur, they shall be handled appropriately in accordance with Chinese law and in conjunction with the relevant provisions of the above three conventions." Article 3, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "This Law shall apply to anyone who commits a crime within the territory of the People's Republic of China, except as otherwise specifically provided by law." Paragraph 3 of the same article provides: "If either the act or the result of a crime occurs within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the crime shall be deemed to have been committed within the territory of the People's Republic of China." Accordingly, on March 4, 1986, the Harbin Intermediate People's Lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a public trial of the case.

The following facts were found upon trial: On December 19, 1985, the defendant Alimuradov Shamil Haji-ogly, together with the captain Abramyan V.S. and other crew members, operated flight No. 101/435 of the Yakutsk Civil Aviation Administration, flying a An-24 civil passenger aircraft, registration number 47845, within the territory of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics. When boarding, the defendant brought a folding knife and a long strip of manganese steel weighing 2.8 kilograms into the cockpit, which he had prepared in advance. At approximately 7:30 a.m. Beijing time, the aircraft, carrying 38 passengers, departed from Yakutsk for Irkutsk. At approximately 12:30 p.m., when the aircraft was flying over the coordinates of 118°06'00" East Longitude and 52°40'00" North Latitude, the defendant took advantage of the navigator Zhikharev S.V. going to the restroom, and under the pretext of a mechanical malfunction in the cabin, tricked the flight engineer Osipov F.I. out of the cockpit. He then immediately locked the cockpit door, disengaged the autopilot, and, wielding the knife, threatened the captain Abramyan V.S. who was flying the aircraft, saying: "Behave yourself, or I will kill you." He forced the captain to fly towards China. The captain immediately activated the alarm signal. When the defendant discovered this, he forced the captain to turn off the signal. The captain was compelled to change course, causing the aircraft to fly into the territorial airspace of the People's Republic of China. At approximately 2:30 p.m., the aircraft landed in a farmland in Changjigang Township, Gannan County, Heilongjiang Province, China.

The above facts are confirmed by the record of the crime scene inspection, technical appraisal conclusions, witness testimony, physical evidence, and other evidence. The defendant also confessed to the facts. The evidence is true, sufficient, and adequate for identification.

The Harbin Intermediate People's Court held at trial: The defendant Alimuradov Shamil Haji-ogly, by means of violence and coercion, hijacked a civil aircraft in flight, causing it to fly into Chinese territory. His act endangered public safety, constituted a crime, and should be punished. In accordance with Article 79 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "where a crime is not expressly provided for in the Specific Provisions of this Law, conviction and sentencing may be made by analogy to the most similar article in the Specific Provisions of this Law," and by analogy to Article 107 of the Criminal Law, the defendant Alimuradov Shamil Haji-ogly was sentenced to eight years' imprisonment for the crime of aircraft hijacking.

The defendant Alimuradov Shamil Haji-ogly did not appeal.

In accordance with the procedures for cases applying analogy, the Heilongjiang High People's Court, after a comprehensive review of the case, found that the facts of the crime committed by Alimuradov Shamil Haji-ogly as determined in the original judgment were clear, the evidence was true and sufficient, the application of the law was correct, and the trial proceedings were lawful. It agreed with the conviction and sentencing by analogy by the Harbin Intermediate People's Court against Alimuradov Shamil Haji-ogly. On March 18, 1986, the Heilongjiang High People's Lawfully reported the case to the Supreme People's Court for approval.

Upon review, the Supreme People's Court found that the judgment of the Harbin Intermediate People's Court of Heilongjiang Province determined that the facts of the crime of aircraft hijacking by the defendant Alimuradov Shamil Haji-ogly were clear, the evidence was true and sufficient, and the conviction and sentencing by analogy to Article 107 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China were appropriate. Following discussion and decision by the Adjudication Committee on March 28, 1986, it was ruled to approve the criminal judgment of the Harbin Intermediate People's Court sentencing the defendant Alimuradov Shamil Haji-ogly to eight years' imprisonment for the crime of aircraft hijacking.
